name: LoRa over a GNU Radio flowgraph
why: The adapter kind that is not a program: a GNU Radio flowgraph, satisfying the same samples-in-records-out contract as rtl_433, with the difference that what must be installed is a module inside an interpreter rather than a name on PATH. It also pins the one adapter whose sample rate is not a constant — LoRa is sampled at a whole multiple of its bandwidth, so the bandwidth parameter decides what the decoder is fed, and a static `wants` would have starved every setting but the default.

expect.note: The frame count is not pinned and neither is the payload length. The capture is three transmissions, gr-lora_sdr finds each more than once at the tail of the zero padding, and the last one runs off the end of the span a byte or two short — all of which is its own frame detection doing its job on a span that was cut somewhere. What matters is that every record carries the same payload and the same parameters.
